title: Adaptive SLO Stewardship for Burst-Prone Conversational Routes with Cross-Region Escrow
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Problem: Several conversational routes (chat-streaming and short-turn assistant flows) exhibit highly bursty traffic that causes asymmetric regional overloads during marketing events. Existing SLOs are static and tied to region-level error budgets; when a region degrades we either over-eject traffic or allow quality regressions. Goal: define per-endpoint and per-model SLIs that capture latency, availability, and quality for conversational routes; create an adaptive policy that allows temporary cross-region error-budget escrow and repayment, plus an automated circuit-breaker and token-aware load-shedding strategy. This ticket produces: (1) canonical SLI definitions for conversational endpoints and model variants, (2) an error-budget escrow policy with borrowing and repayment rules, (3) circuit-breaker thresholds and phased actions (soft degrade -> fallback model -> hard reject), (4) load-shedding algorithms prioritized by customer tier and promptset criticality, (5) runbooks and dashboards for on-call and SRE to exercise in drills and incidents.
acceptance_criteria: Canonical SLI document published referencing exact metric names (request.success, request.latency_ms, eval.promptset_pass_rate) and calculation windows
Error-budget escrow policy implemented in control-plane with unit tests and a simulated soak test showing correct borrow/repay behavior
Circuit-breaker state machine implemented and wired into the routing layer with documented thresholds for soft/hard breaks
Load-shedding strategy implemented for conversational routes: token-aware preemption and fallback-to-quantized-model logic with telemetry enabled
On-call runbook and postmortem template updated; at least one incident drill executed using the new policies
Dashboards and alerting created: error-budget burn-rate, escrow balance per-region, circuit-breaker transitions, and top-10 shed routes

notes:
SLI definitions (summary):
  - Availability SLI: fraction of requests returning 200-like success within 2s (stream-close for streaming requests) computed over sliding 5m and 1h windows.
  - Latency SLI: p50/p95/p99 of response time (ms), measured client-facing and at model-inference boundary.
  - Quality SLI: promptset_pass_rate computed against curated promptset per-route; threshold defaults at 95% but tunable per-model.
  - Composite SLO: weighted combination = 0.6*availability + 0.25*(1 - normalized_p99_latency) + 0.15*quality_pass_rate for high-priority routes.

Error-budget escrow concept: regions hold a local error-budget (EB). During transient overload, a region may borrow from a sacrificial escrow pool (cross-region) up to X% of its EB. Borrowed EB must be repaid within a repayment window (default 72h) by throttling non-critical traffic and applying prioritized shedding. Repayment is enforced by automatic rate-plan adjustments and accounting in control-plane ledger.

Circuit-breaker phases: soft-degrade (start at 80% EB burn over 10m): enable light-weight mitigations (lower batch-size, increase KV cache prefetch), degrade non-essential routes; fallback-model (90% EB burn or sustained p99 > 3s): route to quantized or smaller variants; hard-reject (>=95% EB burn or critical error spike): reject non-SLA traffic and trigger PagerDuty. Transitions emit events to event-bus and Console.

Load-shedding policy: token-aware shedding that estimates per-request token cost and picks victims by (priority_score, estimated_tokens, historical_quality_impact). Prioritize shedding anonymous/free-tier first, then background jobs, then interactive low-tier customers. Preserve pinned/enterprise routes (tenant_exempt_list).

Trade-offs: escrow increases availability but temporarily concentrates risk on repayment phase; complex accounting required. Quality SLI burndown must be measured separately to avoid silent regressions when falling back to smaller models.
Open questions: default escrow percent per-region? suggested 20% initial; repayment enforcement granularity (per-tenant vs global)? needs PM decision.
